steps.say: Continuous treatment with oral NSAIDs at maximum anti-inflammatory doses is recommended as first-line pharmacological therapy for symptomatic active axial spondyloarthritis, providing rapid symptomatic relief and reducing inflammatory spinal stiffness. Full anti-inflammatory doses first, not analgesic sips.
steps.tx: Continuous treatment with oral **NSAIDs** at maximum anti-inflammatory doses is recommended as **first-line** pharmacological therapy for symptomatic active **axial spondyloarthritis**, providing rapid symptomatic relief and reducing inflammatory spinal stiffness. Full anti-inflammatory doses first, not analgesic sips. Doses are pushed to the anti-inflammatory range, not kept at simple analgesic levels, and response is judged within weeks.

steps.say: Conventional synthetic DMARDs such as methotrexate, sulfasalazine and leflunomide have proven lack of efficacy for purely axial inflammatory disease and are not recommended for isolated sacroiliitis or spondylitis. Limbs differ from spine here.
steps.tx: Conventional synthetic DMARDs (**methotrexate**, **sulfasalazine**, **leflunomide**) have proven **lack of efficacy** for purely **axial** inflammatory disease and are not recommended for isolated **sacroiliitis** or spondylitis. Limbs differ from spine here. This inefficacy is proven, not assumed. Save these drugs for peripheral joint disease where they work.

steps.say: Sulfasalazine at two to three grams daily is conditionally recommended only for patients with prominent peripheral arthritis or concomitant inflammatory bowel disease associated with axial spondyloarthritis. Isolated spine excludes it.
steps.tx: **Sulfasalazine** (**2 to 3 g daily**) is conditionally recommended only for patients with prominent **peripheral arthritis** or concomitant **inflammatory bowel disease** associated with axial spondyloarthritis. Isolated spine excludes it. The bowel or the peripheral joints must dominate the picture. Reassess often, since axial symptoms alone never justify it.

rows: Prominent peripheral arthritis or IBD with axSpA

steps.say: Patients with persistently active axial SpA with ASDAS at or above two point one or BASDAI at or above four despite trials of at least two different NSAIDs over four weeks qualify for escalation to a biologic DMARD or targeted synthetic DMARD. Two drugs plus high scores are the gate.
steps.tx: Patients with persistently active axial SpA (**ASDAS >=2.1** or **BASDAI >=4**) despite trials of at least **two different NSAIDs** over **4 weeks** qualify for escalation to a **biologic** DMARD or targeted synthetic DMARD. Two drugs plus high scores are the gate.

rows: ASDAS 2.1 or more, BASDAI 4 or more
At least two different NSAIDs over 4 weeks

steps.tx: The MRI shows bright **bone marrow oedema** lighting both **sacroiliac joints**, labelled as active axial disease with biologic indicated. This is the escalation point taught after continuous **NSAIDs** fail to control inflammation. Such imaging proof of activity supports starting a **TNF alpha inhibitor** or IL 17 blocker. For exams, link persistent symptoms plus marrow oedema to biologic therapy.
steps.say: This scan of the pelvis shows bright signal from inflamed marrow on both sides of the sacroiliac joints. That is active sacroiliitis in axial disease that has not settled with regular anti inflammatory tablets. The lesson teaches that such persistent active disease calls for a biologic drug. Linking marrow swelling on MRI to escalation should guide the exam answer.

vis.alt: Coronal MRI shows bright bone marrow oedema across both sacroiliac joints marking active axial disease.
vis.caption: Active sacroiliitis with marrow oedema prompts biologic escalation. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: First-line biologic choices include TNF inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies infliximab, adalimumab, golimumab and certolizumab or soluble receptor etanercept, and interleukin seventeen A inhibitors secukinumab and ixekizumab, both demonstrating equivalent clinical efficacy. Equal benefit, differing baggage.
steps.tx: First-line biologic choices include **TNF inhibitors** (monoclonal antibodies: **infliximab**, **adalimumab**, **golimumab**, **certolizumab**; or soluble receptor: **etanercept**) and **IL-17A inhibitors** (**secukinumab**, **ixekizumab**), both demonstrating equivalent clinical efficacy. Equal benefit, differing baggage. Choice between them rests on comorbidity and access rather than superior joint efficacy. Both beat NSAIDs alone when disease stays active.

steps.say: In patients with concomitant recurrent anterior uveitis or active inflammatory bowel disease, monoclonal anti-TNF antibodies infliximab, adalimumab and certolizumab are strongly preferred over etanercept or interleukin seventeen inhibitors. Eye or bowel comorbidity is the monoclonal vote.
steps.tx: In patients with concomitant recurrent **anterior uveitis** or active **inflammatory bowel disease**, monoclonal anti-TNF antibodies (**infliximab**, **adalimumab**, **certolizumab**) are strongly preferred over **etanercept** or **IL-17 inhibitors**. Eye or bowel comorbidity is the monoclonal vote. Etanercept lacks efficacy in eye and bowel disease. Interleukin-17 blockade shares that limitation.

steps.say: Bimekizumab, a dual monoclonal antibody neutralizing both interleukin seventeen A and interleukin seventeen F, and oral JAK inhibitors tofacitinib and upadacitinib are approved options for active axial SpA failing TNF inhibitors. New lanes are open after old roadblocks.
steps.tx: **Bimekizumab**, a dual monoclonal antibody neutralizing both **IL-17A** and **IL-17F**, and oral JAK inhibitors (**tofacitinib**, **upadacitinib**) are approved options for active axial SpA failing **TNF inhibitors**. New lanes are open after old roadblocks. These options carry their own cautions. JAK inhibitors need the same cardiovascular vigilance as in rheumatoid arthritis.

steps.say: Structured regular physical therapy and home-based spinal extension exercises are essential non-pharmacological pillars to preserve spinal mobility, maintain thoracic chest expansion, and prevent spinal kyphotic deformity. Pills calm fire, movement keeps shape.
steps.tx: Structured regular **physical therapy** and home-based **spinal extension** exercises are essential non-pharmacological pillars to preserve **spinal mobility**, maintain thoracic **chest expansion**, and prevent spinal **kyphotic deformity**. Pills calm fire, movement keeps shape. Supervised sessions start the program, then home extension continues it. Stopping exercise lets stiffness reclaim the spine.
